answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making trust a web, not a token. An identity earns standing only through completed work exchanges with distinct counterparties, and each exchange leaves a pigment in the public record, like dye spreading through an ocean. A newcomer must wander that ocean gathering real partners, while a forger's sockpuppets can only trade with each other, forming a tight clique cut off from the main web. Every extra fake identity needs fresh, real counterparties willing to risk their own standing to vouch, so the cost grows with each fake and cannot be bought in bulk.
